passage: On Saturday, Mohit, five, dropped his shoulders when the picnic was cancelled because of rain and sat with his chin on his knees. His mother Sudha said, "You're disappointed. I am too." He nodded. On Tuesday he lost the sticker prize at school, scowled and refused his tea. "Another letdown," said Sudha. "It's okay to feel it." The next Saturday, when the swing was broken, Mohit said, "I'm disappointed," kicked the mat once, and chose another game.

qa.q: Why was the picnic cancelled?
qa.a: Because of rain.

qa.q: What was Mohit feeling on Tuesday when he refused his tea?
qa.a: Disappointment at losing the prize, shown by his scowl and refusing tea. He might also have been tired.

qa.q: How did Sudha help Mohit with his letdowns?
qa.a: She named the feeling and let it be there without rushing it away.

qa.q: How might Sudha feel about the cancelled picnic?
qa.a: Disappointed herself, since she said "I am too". 🙂

grounding: Shows a preschooler sulking after disappointments and learning through naming that letdowns pass.

passage: At the bus stop, the bus to the fair was full and left without them. Dilnaz, five, dropped her shoulders and pushed out her lip. "But I wanted the balloons." Her aunt Maria crouched beside her in the rain. "You're disappointed. Me too. We'll have to wait for the next bus." Dilnaz kicked a pebble and sulked for a moment. Then she leaned on Maria's arm. "Can we watch for it?"

qa.q: What did Dilnaz want at the fair?
qa.a: The balloons.

qa.q: What was Dilnaz feeling at the bus stop?
qa.a: Disappointment, shown by her dropped shoulders, pushed-out lip and kicked pebble.

qa.q: What did Maria do that helped?
qa.a: She named the disappointment, shared it and let Dilnaz feel it without rushing her.

qa.q: How might Maria feel about the missed bus?
qa.a: Sorry too, since she said "Me too" and stayed beside Dilnaz in the rain.

grounding: Shows a preschooler protesting a missed outing, with an adult naming the disappointment while waiting in the rain.

passage: The zoo trip was planned for Sunday, and Vijay had packed his binoculars on Saturday night. On Sunday morning, it poured. Tanuja said, “Sorry, beta, the zoo is cancelled today.” Vijay dropped onto the sofa, shoulders slumped, lower lip out. “It's not fair. I wanted to see the tiger.” Tanuja sat beside him. “You're really disappointed. You were so excited.” He nodded, eyes wet. She didn't rush to fix it. After a while he sighed, picked up the binoculars, and started spying on the pigeons.

qa.q: What had Vijay packed on Saturday night?
qa.a: His binoculars.

qa.q: What was Vijay feeling when he dropped onto the sofa?
qa.a: He was disappointed and let down that the zoo trip was cancelled, especially after being so excited.

qa.q: What did Tanuja do that helped Vijay get through the letdown?
qa.a: She named his disappointment and let it pass without rushing to fix it.

qa.q: What would change if Tanuja had said “Stop sulking, it's only a zoo”?
qa.a: Vijay might feel dismissed and stay upset longer, instead of recovering by himself.

grounding: A preschooler sulks when a zoo trip is cancelled, and his mother names the disappointment and lets it pass.

passage:
“Papa, I didn't win.”
Ritu came out of the school hall, shoulders drooping, holding her drawing.
Joseph crouched. “The drawing competition?”
“The prize went to Arun. Mine was better.”
“You're disappointed.”
“Very.” She scuffed her shoe.
“That feels bad. You worked on that jungle all week.”
“Can we go home?”
“Yes. And shall we put your jungle on the wall?”
Ritu looked at her drawing. “…Okay. Next to the window.”
On the way home, she started humming again.

qa.q: What had Ritu drawn?
qa.a: A jungle.

qa.q: What was Ritu feeling as she came out with drooping shoulders?
qa.a: She felt disappointed and a bit resentful that she didn't win the prize.

qa.q: How did Joseph help Ritu handle the letdown?
qa.a: He named her disappointment, acknowledged her week of work and offered to put the drawing on the wall.

qa.q: How might Joseph feel when Ritu starts humming again?
qa.a: He is likely relieved and glad that her disappointment has passed.

grounding: A preschooler is disappointed at losing a prize, and her father names the feeling and lets it pass.

passage:
Sports day note, written by Reena, KG teacher.
Vikas came last in the running race. He walked off the track with his shoulders dropped and sat with his back to everyone. When I sat beside him, he said, “I'm always last.” I said, “You're disappointed. You really wanted to win.” He nodded and picked at the grass. I didn't try to cheer him up straight away. Ten minutes later he stood up and cheered loudly for his friend in the next race. The letdown passed.

qa.q: Where did Vikas come in the running race?
qa.a: Last.

qa.q: What was Vikas feeling when he sat with his back to everyone?
qa.a: He felt disappointed and discouraged, believing he's always last.

qa.q: Why was it wise for Reena not to cheer Vikas up straight away?
qa.a: Letting the disappointment be named and pass on its own teaches him that letdowns are survivable.

qa.q: How might Vikas's friend feel hearing him cheer?
qa.a: The friend would likely feel supported and happy to have Vikas cheering.

grounding: The teacher's note shows a preschooler's disappointment after losing a race being named and allowed to pass.

passage:
Arohi had worn her green frock since morning. The mela in the next village! Then Saurabh bhaiya came back from the field shaking his head. "The tractor's broken, Arohi. No mela today."

Arohi's shoulders dropped. She kicked the charpai leg and shouted, "You promised!" Then she sat on the step with her face in her knees. Bhaiya sat down beside her. "You're really disappointed. Me too." He said nothing else. After a while she leaned on his arm, and together they watched the goats.

qa.q: Why was there no mela trip that day?
qa.a: The tractor was broken.

qa.q: What does Arohi kicking the charpai and shouting "You promised!" suggest?
qa.a: She was most likely deeply disappointed, with some anger at Saurabh bhaiya for the broken promise. Hiding her face in her knees shows the letdown sinking in.

qa.q: Which choice helped Arohi, and why?
qa.a: Bhaiya named the feeling and then sat quietly with her instead of lecturing, which let the disappointment pass on its own.

qa.q: How does Saurabh bhaiya feel about the cancelled trip?
qa.a: He is disappointed too, as he says "Me too", and may feel sorry that he could not keep his promise.

grounding: It shows a preschooler's drooping shoulders and protest when a fair trip is cancelled, and an adult naming the disappointment and letting it pass.
